summary: BLM-administered Nevada lookout in Lincoln County, standing and seasonally staffed; the register dates it 1962 and UTV Guide 1964.

facts.design: modified R-6 flattop cab, 14 by 14 feet with a catwalk and slightly slanting windows, on an 8-foot concrete block base; FFLA lists a 2-story cab

staffing.status: typically manned May to October; the only remaining staffed structure among Nevada's three standing lookouts

visit.trail_note: rugged forest roads best suited to high-clearance vehicles, per UTV Guide

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1962 and describes the cab. UTV Guide gives 1964. Neither source explains the difference, so the story reports both dates without choosing one.
The register places the lookout in the Clover Mountains. UTV Guide places it deep within the Spring Mountains. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Built year is unresolved: the register says 1962 and UTV Guide says 1964. The Review-Journal article ('It's lonely at the top for Nevada's last fire lookout') returned HTTP 500 on every fetch attempt, so it is not used; it is likely the best source for staffing history and should be retried. A Facebook post by Eastern Nevada Interagency Fire repeats 1964, but Facebook was not readable, so it is not cited. No fire history or rebuild information was found in readable sources, so the story has no fire section. The access level is omitted because no source says whether visitors may enter the cab. Staffing as_of is undated because UTV Guide shows no publication date. Elevation (2,265 m per register) and coordinates match the brief; the FFLA listing gives longitude -114.46730, a small difference from the register's -114.468050.
